verdict.rationale: Mailgun ships its own rule-based background automation: inbound Routes apply user-defined forwarding or storage rules automatically, and it automatically handles unsubscribes, complaints, and bounces. A community user corroborates the inbound rules. Webhooks, the MCP server (conversational, on demand), and the n8n and GitHub Actions automations run in other platforms or are developer building blocks, so they earn no credit here. missing for 10: general-purpose user-configurable background workflows beyond inbound routing and suppression handling, native scheduling or recurring automations, any agentic or AI-driven autonomous execution, and depth documentation of automation triggers and actions.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Define rules for handling incoming emails, such as forwarding to a specific address or storing the email.
Automatically handle unsubscribes, complaints, and bounces to maintain a clean email list.
They've got the best inbound handling of all of the services out there in terms of letting you apply rules before the messages hit your servers.
